title: A fan-out that cannot tell dead from empty, or stop

candidates.pattern: Consecutive-failure streak breaker: after N agent deaths in a row, stop spawning and report the unspawned work as NOT_SPAWNED (fail-closed), rather than letting every queued agent launch into a dead dependency.
candidates.failurePrevented: A usage/credit wall kills agents one after another while the fan-out keeps launching: 2026-07-25 all 10 agents 'failed AFTER burning ~687k tokens' (memory reference-fable5-credits-exhausted.md); 'Three usage-limit deaths in a row on SSHD's L0 lane (08-13, 08-14, 08-15)' (memory project-workflow-salvage-pattern.md). pipeline() has no barrier, so on this 8-CPU box (sysctl hw.ncpu → 8; cap = min(16, cpus-2) = 6) six measure agents launch at once and the remaining units plus every refuter (units × lenses) still queue behind them after the wall hits.

A streak trips on the present instead."; :311-313 `if (config.consecutiveFailures() > 0 && streak >= config.consecutiveFailures()) { return toOpen(Reason.CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES); }`; :307 `streak = outcome == FAIL ? streak + 1 : 0;`; conf/application.conf:921 "# llm.breaker.consecutive-failures=3  # failures in a row that open it regardless of the rate; 0 disables"; commit cea0b21f: "from a warm window the breaker needed 50 failed turns, about ten hours of hung turns, before it first turned a call away ... a rate measures the past, a streak measures the present"; app/llm/LlmResilience.java:26-29 records ONE failure per whole retry loop: "Recording per attempt instead would multiply every failure by four".

The runtime `budget` global is a spend ceiling that exists only when a '+500k' directive is given (workflow-authoring skill: 'budget.total is null if no target was set'), not a death gate.
candidates.proposal: agent-harness/harness/workflows/measure-refute.js (symlinked into ~/.claude/workflows, so SSHD gets it): add `let deaths = 0; const MAX_DEATHS = cfg.maxConsecutiveDeaths ?? 2;` and one `spawn(prompt, opts)` wrapper used by both phases: if `deaths >= MAX_DEATHS` return `{ notSpawned: 'breaker open after ' + deaths + ' consecutive deaths' }` without calling agent(); on a live result set `deaths = 0`; on null/throw `deaths++`. Count runtime-level retries as one death (JClaw's one-outcome-per-call rule; the runtime already retries before returning null). Report `notSpawnedCount` in `integrity` and mark those verdicts UNVERIFIED with that reason; fatalCount stays null. Add one test to measure-refute.test.mjs: fake agent dies from call 3 onward → labels.length < units*(1+lenses), integrity matches /breaker open/, status UNVERIFIED, fatalCount null.
candidates.doneCriterion: `node --test harness/workflows/measure-refute.test.mjs` prints the new test PASS, and with the `deaths++` line commented out it prints FAIL (red first). Existing 9 tests still pass.
candidates.cost: ~25 lines of plain JS + 1 test; zero dependencies; zero per-turn tokens; saves up to (units×lenses + queued units) agent launches per wall.
candidates.why: Closes the one wall failure the fail-closed accounting only REPORTS today (it names dead agents but still launches the rest). Streak-of-2 is the whole breaker for a solo run: a rate rule is JClaw's own anti-pattern for low traffic (see antiPatterns).

candidates.pattern: Reason-carrying failure: every breaker transition and every refusal carries WHY (Reason enum with a `manual()` split; ManuallyIsolated vs BreakerOpen), so an operator's stop is never read as the dependency breaking and a diagnosis can be made from the record alone.
candidates.failurePrevented: A dead fan-out whose result cannot say whether the agent hit a usage wall, a budget ceiling, or was skipped by the user — three cases with three different recoveries (wait for reset and resume unedited / narrow the script / nothing to fix). Already bitten in build-loop.sh:96-98: 'a bare cycle header with zero output was undiagnosable (quota death? auth prompt? crash?) in the 07-12 log'.

candidates.ourEvidence: agent-harness/harness/workflows/measure-refute.js:192 `.catch(() => null)` discards the measure error; :195 the reason string is the conflation itself: `'the measure agent returned nothing or threw'`. The refute branch keeps it (:203 `the refute agent threw: ${err.message}`). candidates.proposal: measure-refute.js: `.catch((err) => ({ __dead: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) }))` on the measure stage; UNMEASURED units carry `reason: 'THREW: <msg>'` vs `'DIED_OR_SKIPPED'` vs `'NOT_SPAWNED: <breaker reason>'` (from resilience-gates-1); integrity adds the three counts, e.g. '2 THREW (budget), 3 DIED/SKIPPED, 4 NOT_SPAWNED'. One test: a measure that throws `new Error('budget ceiling')` → `units[i].reason` matches /budget ceiling/ and the unit is still UNMEASURED.

candidates.cost: ~10 lines + 1 test; zero deps; zero per-turn tokens.
candidates.why: The salvage playbook's first step is diagnosis ('inventory ... mine them'); a reason string in the result skips that step. Cheapest change in this list and it is the same lesson build-loop.sh already paid for.

candidates.pattern: Half-open probe: after a trip, admit a bounded number of probes and re-open on the first that fails; close only when all succeed — never relaunch the whole fleet on hope.
candidates.failurePrevented: Relaunching a full fan-out into a wall that has not lifted (three consecutive-day deaths 08-13/14/15 on one lane). Today the advice exists only as prose: memory reference-fable5-credits-exhausted.md:85 'prefer a cheap single-agent probe first if there is any doubt about credit state'; playbooks/crash-resilience.md 'Don't launch a fleet near a limit window' — neither is a mechanism.
candidates.jclawEvidence: app/utils/CircuitBreaker.java:14-17 "after a cooldown it admits a bounded number of probes (HALF_OPEN) and closes once they all succeed, or re-opens on the first one that does not"; :335-339 `takePermit()` caps admitted probes at `halfOpenPermits`; :327-333 `probeReported` re-opens on FAIL or SLOW; conf/application.conf:923 "# llm.breaker.half-open-probes=3    # probes that must all succeed to close it again"; app/llm/LlmResilience.java:192-195 a stranded permit "wedges the breaker shut for good" so the finally block always reports.
candidates.builtAndExercised: test/CircuitBreakerTest.java:192 `halfOpenAdmitsExactlyThePermittedNumberOfProbes`, :205 `halfOpenClosesOnlyAfterEveryProbeSucceeds`, :222 `halfOpenReopensOnTheFirstProbeFailure`, :130 `aProbeFromAnEarlierWindowNeitherClosesNorReopensTheCurrentOne` (JCLAW-1186 stale-probe stamping). Pre-push hook runs them.
candidates.ourEvidence: Prose only (memory line 85; crash-resilience.md). Resume replay is proven — project-workflow-salvage-pattern.md 'resuming unedited replayed 28 agents free' — but pipeline() launches every uncached unit at once (no barrier; concurrency cap 6 here), so the first 6 uncached agents die together on a relaunch into a live wall. grep 'probe' in measure-refute.js and measure-verify.js → 0 hits.
candidates.proposal: measure-refute.js: `args.probeFirst` (default true on any run) — `await spawn(measurePrompt(UNITS[0]))` alone; if it is not a live measurement, return `{ status: 'UNVERIFIED', fatalCount: null, integrity: 'probe unit died; fleet not launched (0 further agents)', units: [...] }`; else run pipeline over UNITS.slice(1) and prepend the probe result. One probe, not JClaw's three: the streak breaker (resilience-gates-1) already re-opens on the next two deaths, and a 3-probe close rule costs 3 serial agents on every healthy run. Test: probe dead → labels.length === 1, status UNVERIFIED.
candidates.doneCriterion: Test PASS/red-first as above; a relaunch into a wall costs exactly ONE agent (visible as 1 label in the journal), not 6.
candidates.cost: ~15 lines + 1 test; adds one agent's wall-clock latency to the front of every run (the probe unit runs alone before the rest start).
candidates.why: Worth having because a wall relaunch has happened three days running, but the latency cost is real on an ADD-friendly workflow, so it is a single probe and an arg, not a 3-permit state machine. Ordering note: adopt after resilience-gates-1, which supplies `spawn()`.

candidates.pattern: Orphan-process sweep by command-line signature: list candidates, EXCLUDE live ones explicitly, SIGTERM, wait, escalate to SIGKILL, and kill the whole tree (descendants snapshotted before the parent dies).
candidates.failurePrevented: Leaked processes from dead runs thrashing an 8 GB machine (already bitten: ~12 orphaned vite/http.server/node processes 4-5 days old on 2026-09-10), and the opposite failure JClaw hit on 2026-09-14 — a sweep that kills a LIVE run because the signature matched.

Sweep by process signature instead"; jclaw.sh:3124 `candidates=$(pgrep -f "application.path=${SCRIPT_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true)`; :3127-3129 `case "$(ps -o command= -p "$pid" ...)" in *-Dplay.id=test*) continue ;;`; :3135-3141 `kill "$pid"` ... `sleep 3` ... `echo "pid $pid ignored SIGTERM — escalating to kill -9."`. Tree kill: app/services/SubagentRegistry.java:266-268 `var descendants = proc.descendants().toList(); proc.destroyForcibly(); descendants.forEach(ProcessHandle::destroyForcibly);` with :247-248 "descendants first (snapshotted before the parent dies so the whole tree is reaped)". Windows fallback fails loud not silent: :3120-3122 "the signature sweep is skipped there rather than reporting \"no orphans\"".
candidates.builtAndExercised: Built. Commit 8cf33aa3 (2026-09-14) "fix(jclaw.sh): keep the orphan-JVM sweep off running test servers" — message: "restarting JClaw while tests ran killed the test server ... the push was rejected after 19.5 minutes ... Verified: ... The sweep ran against two detached dummy processes ... the edited version killed only the play.id=prod process and left the test process running." The Java tree-kill has no dedicated unit test I found (grep for `descendants` in test/ was not run); the shell sweep is verified by the commit's manual run, not a committed test.
candidates.ourEvidence: Searched SSHD 1-1 and agent-harness (`grep -rn -i -E "orphan|pkill|lsof|ps aux|ps -ef"` over *.md,*.js,*.mjs,*.ts,*.sh,*.json,pre-commit*): zero hits outside npc test names. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ship-bar.md, settings.json: no orphan/process rule, no SessionEnd/Stop hook (settings.json has only a UserPromptSubmit hook). The only record is memory project-orphaned-processes-and-tunnel.md: "~12 ORPHANED PROCESSES on a machine with 64 MB free RAM ... no auditor thought to run `ps` until asked". Live measurement during this study: `ps -eo pid,etime,command | grep -E 'vite|http\.server|run-pipeline'` -> pid 75716 `Python -m http.server 8899 --bind 127.0.0.1` etime 02:03:23, spawned by a `/bin/sh -c ... &` tool call — the leak pattern recurs today. We DO kill a process group in one place: agent-harness/harness/chaos/chaos.mjs:184 `process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM') // the whole group: npx → runner → workers` (spawned `detached: true`, :215); SSHD scripts/gates/chaos.ts:114-118 uses `execFileSync('npx', ['vitest', ...], { timeout: 900_000 })` which signals only the direct child — RESUME_HERE already lists this as a hole not yet ported.
candidates.proposal: agent-harness `harness/sweep-orphans.sh` (~40 lines, POSIX sh + pgrep/ps only, zero deps), symlinked into SSHD `scripts/`. Default is DRY-RUN: print pid, etime, command for processes matching a signature list (`vite`, `http.server`, `node .*run-`, `cloudflared tunnel --url`) older than `--min-age` (default 6h), EXCLUDING any pid whose ancestor chain contains a live `claude` process (JClaw's `play.id=test` exclusion, generalised). `--kill` sends SIGTERM to the process GROUP (`kill -- -$pgid`), sleeps 3, escalates to `kill -9` and prints which pids ignored TERM. No hook, no per-turn tokens; run it from the session-kickoff playbook line and after any workflow death.
candidates.doneCriterion: 1) With the 8899 http.server running: `sh harness/sweep-orphans.sh` lists it and exits 0 without killing (ps count unchanged). 2) `sh harness/sweep-orphans.sh --kill` -> `ps -p 75716` returns 1. 3) A dummy `sleep 99999 &` started from the current claude session is LISTED as excluded and never killed. 4) A test (`sweep-orphans.test.mjs`) spawns two detached dummies (one under a fake 'claude' parent) and asserts only the unparented one dies — the same two-dummy proof JClaw's commit describes.
candidates.cost: ~1 h to write + test; 0 tokens/turn (not a hook); zero runtime dependencies; one new file in agent-harness plus a symlink in SSHD.
candidates.why: The failure has already bitten this machine and nothing in our three locations detects it — a clear GAP. JClaw's version is JVM-specific (`application.path=`), so adapt the SHAPE (signature list + age + live-exclusion + TERM->KILL + group kill), not the code. Dry-run default and live-exclusion are non-negotiable: JClaw's own sweep killed a live test server the first time it was wrong, and our chaos.mjs already proves the group-kill idiom works here.

candidates.pattern: Every spawned run carries an absolute ceiling set by the OPERATOR, not by the run itself, independent of activity — on top of any activity-based budget.
candidates.failurePrevented: A runaway child that keeps producing activity (or keeps taking turns) and never stops — the 'node with no stop condition' our global rule calls a bug. JClaw's idle budget alone could never trip on an active child, so the ceiling was added as a separate, LLM-unsettable bound.
candidates.jclawEvidence: app/tools/SubagentSpawnTool.java:140-148 "JCLAW-424: operator-controlled absolute wall-clock ceiling on a single subagent run, independent of activity — the runaway guard the idle budget (which an active child never trips) cannot provide. NOT settable by the spawning LLM. {@code 0} disables the ceiling" `MAX_WALLCLOCK_KEY = "subagent.maxWallClockSeconds"`, `DEFAULT_MAX_WALLCLOCK_SECONDS = 1800`. Enforcement: app/tools/SubagentSyncRunner.java:121-124 `if (System.nanoTime() - startNanos > ceilingNanos) { return stopChildOnTimeout(future, runId, "Subagent run exceeded the absolute %d-second ceiling"...`. docs/user-guide/subagents.md:124 "Set it to `0` to wait indefinitely (not recommended for an unattended instance)."
candidates.builtAndExercised: Built and tested: test/SubagentSpawnToolTest.java:536 `void absoluteCeilingTimesOutEvenWhenActive()` — "1s ceiling, huge idle budget, constant touches" asserts `SubagentRun.Status.TIMEOUT` and the reason contains "ceiling"; :471 `activityKeepsRunAlivePastIdleBudget()`; :520 `idleRunTimesOutWhenSilent()`. Commit 8bc085e0 "JCLAW-424: idle/activity-based subagent run timeout + absolute ceiling".
candidates.ourEvidence: Workflow runtime (workflow-authoring reference, loaded this study): `budget` is a HARD ceiling ("once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw") but only when the user passes a '+500k'-style directive (`budget.total` is null otherwise); a 1000-agent lifetime cap and a concurrency cap of min(16, CPUs-2) — on this box `sysctl hw.ncpu` = 8 -> 6 concurrent. `agent()` opts are `label, phase, schema, model, effort, isolation, agentType` — no per-agent timeout or turn cap exists to set. The one run we spawn ourselves has the knob and leaves it OFF: SSHD scripts/build-loop.sh:41 "LOOP_MAX_TURNS  optional --max-turns per cycle (hung-cycle insurance)" and :111 `${LOOP_MAX_TURNS:+--max-turns "$LOOP_MAX_TURNS"}` — unset by default, so an unattended cycle has no ceiling but the geometric sleep after it ends. chaos runners DO have one: agent-harness chaos.mjs:25 `const TEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; SSHD chaos.ts:118 `timeout: 900_000`.
candidates.proposal: SSHD scripts/build-loop.sh: make the ceiling the default, overridable — replace the two lines with `MAX_TURNS=${LOOP_MAX_TURNS:-80}` and pass `--max-turns "$MAX_TURNS"` unconditionally (0 = off, documented in the header). Stamp the value into the cycle header line written to loop.log so a postmortem shows the bound the cycle ran under.
candidates.doneCriterion: `grep -n -- '--max-turns' scripts/build-loop.sh` shows an unconditional flag with a numeric default; `sh -n scripts/build-loop.sh` exits 0; a dry cycle header in docs/loop/loop.log carries `max-turns=80`. Ceiling proven by running one cycle with `LOOP_MAX_TURNS=2` and reading `[loop] claude exit=` after it stops early.
candidates.why: Our own global rule says 'A node with no stop condition is a bug' and build-loop.sh — the only spawner we control end-to-end, explicitly meant to run unattended overnight — ships with the ceiling off. JClaw's design point that matters is that the ceiling is the operator's default, not an opt-in the run can forget. Nothing to adopt for Workflow agents: the runtime owns their bounds and exposes no per-agent knob.

candidates.failurePrevented: One call saturating the executor — on our machine, a large units x lenses product queueing hundreds of agents on 6 concurrent slots of an 8 GB box, burning a full usage window with no way to bank early results.

candidates.pattern: In-flight markers are reconciled by AGE, not trusted: anything still marked RUNNING after a restart and older than a grace window is stamped DEAD with a distinct reason; a marker younger than the grace window is left alone.
